extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, rulemaking staff, and public comment submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical guidance for submitting and processing public comments in federal notice-and-comment rulemakings, with criteria for identifying fraudulent/mass submissions and recommendations for agencies and commenters to improve authenticity and substantive engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass / Fraudulent Comment Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Many high-profile rulemakings have received fraudulent comments; stolen identities used to submit comments without consent; bots and automated systems generated millions of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat unusually large volumes or sudden surges of comments as a potential sign of fraud or automated campaigns; investigate provenance and patterns before treating volume as reflective of public consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical text across submissions (duplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identical text across submissions is a mass campaign indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deduplication and similarity-detection tools; for commenters, avoid using campaign templates verbatim—customize and make each submission substantively distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity attribution and impersonation concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Stolen identities used to submit comments without consent; agencies lack robust authentication mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should implement stronger identity-verification mechanisms; commenters should submit from clearly identified accounts and include contact/personal details that demonstrate authentic identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission patterns inconsistent with claimed identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission metadata or patterns that do not match the claimed identity (e.g., geographic or timing discrepancies) indicate potential fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze metadata and submission patterns (timestamps, IPs, account creation) to flag suspicious submissions; commenters should provide context/details that align with their claimed identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: No engagement with specific provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that do not engage with specific regulatory provisions are indicative of low-quality or campaign signaled input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage or require commenters to cite and discuss particular provisions, sections, or regulatory text and explain how the rule would affect them or relevant stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: No verifiable factual content
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments lacking verifiable facts (unsupported assertions) are less substantive and more likely to be dismissed as part of a mass campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require or favor comments that provide verifiable factual claims, citations, data, or evidence; commenters should include sources or documentation to corroborate statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty distinguishing AI-generated, bot, and human comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies face challenges distinguishing AI-generated, bot, and human comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop detection methods and authentication protocols; consider signals such as linguistic patterns, metadata, and submission behavior to differentiate automated content from human-authored content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass campaigns blur substantive vs. preference signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass campaigns can make it difficult to tell whether comments represent substantive engagement with regulatory text or merely express a preference through volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt criteria that prioritize substantive engagement (specific argumentation, evidence, provision-level discussion) over raw counts of similar expressions of preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve identity verification mechanisms (agency obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should improve identity verification mechanisms to reduce impersonation and fraudulent submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider account-based submissions, multi-factor authentication, identity attestation, or other practical verification steps while balancing accessibility and privacy concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better deduplication tools (agency obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should deploy or improve tools to detect and deduplicate mass or identical submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement automated similarity detection, clustering, and manual review processes to identify template-based campaigns and quantify distinct substantive inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced transparency about comment processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should increase transparency about how comments were processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish methodologies for comment intake, deduplication, filtering, and how comment weight or consideration was determined; disclose how mass campaigns were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination across agencies on common standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should coordinate on common standards for handling mass/fraudulent comments and authentication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop interagency best practices and shared tools/standards to ensure consistent treatment of public comments across rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement against parties submitting fraudulent comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should pursue enforcement against parties submitting fraudulent comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use legal and administrative remedies where appropriate to deter identity theft, impersonation, and orchestrated fraud in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit from clearly identified email/account (commenter guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comment from clearly identified email/account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a recognizable contact or account that can be associated with the commenter; avoid anonymous or throwaway accounts if you want the comment treated as substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make comments substantively distinct from campaign templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it substantively distinct from any campaign template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalize language, include unique arguments or evidence, and avoid copying mass-distributed text; bespoke comments are more likely to be recognized as authentic substantive input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include personal details demonstrating authentic identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Include personal details that demonstrate authentic identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share relevant personal or professional information (e.g., role, local impacts, firsthand experience) that corroborates the commenter's stake or expertise while mindful of privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide verifiable factual claims (commenter guidance)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite data, studies, documents, or firsthand evidence where possible; attach or reference supporting materials to strengthen credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with specific regulatory provisions (commenter guidance)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote, reference, or discuss particular sections, proposed language, or regulatory mechanisms and explain the practical effects or suggested changes.
